newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil actor accuses ex-wife in soap opera murder.
newsitem.headline: Brazil actor accuses ex-wife in soap opera murder.

text.p: A Brazilian actor accused of murdering his screen lover on Wednesday said it was his jealous former wife who committed the murder.

Guilherme de Padua, testifying at the start of a high-profile trial that has gripped millions of Brazilian soap opera fans, said his ex-wife Paula Thomaz killed actress Daniela Perez four years ago by stabbing her repeatedly with a pair of scissors.
"Paula was shouting 'Go away Guilherme, leave that woman, leave that tramp'," he said.
He said he watched Thomaz repeatedly stab Perez as she lay unconscious on the ground with a look "that wasn't anger ... but like she didn't really want to do it but had to."
De Padua, a former male stripper turned soap opera star, and Thomaz are jointly charged with murder.
But prosecutors and defence lawyers agreed to separate the trials of the two defendants and the proceedings, expected to continue for several days, opened with de Padua taking the witness stand.
In the soap opera "De Corpo e Alma" (of Body and Soul), 27-year-old de Padua played the brooding boyfriend of sexy teenager Yasmin, played by Perez.

He originally confessed to murdering Perez, who was 22 years old at the time, but later accused Thomaz, now aged 23, of carrying out the stabbing in a fit of jealousy. The two were divorced soon after de Padua was imprisoned pending his trial.

The 1992 killing eclipsed news of the on-going impeachment of former president Fernando Collor and spawned calls for a crackdown in Brazil's justice system, where well-connected defendants often go unpunished.

De Padua and Thomaz face a maximum sentence of 30 years in jail if convicted. But under Brazilian law, first-time offenders can be released after serving a sixth of their term. Both defendants have already spent the past four years behind bars.
